one_month_reasoning: onsemi has not confirmed its Q3 date; it is expected around Nov 2, just outside the window ending Oct 29, with a small risk it lands earlier. Inside the window: the Oct 28 FOMC decision (meeting Oct 27-28), where prediction markets priced ~69% odds of another hike as of Sep 29 (supervisor, defirate/CNBC), which I missed in round 1. Because a hike is mostly priced, it adds variance more than drift. Also in the window are value-chain read-throughs: Tesla Q3 deliveries (~Oct 2) and earnings (late Oct), TI (~Oct 20-21) and NXP/STMicro (~Oct 22-28) Q3 reports and Q4 guides, and September EV sales data. Peer tone is constructive (TI, NXP, Infineon raised), but the high-voltage EV niche is weak (NA EV sales -33% y/y in August), so the two roughly cancel. I use a symmetric lognormal centred on $75.95 with ~17% one-month sigma, slightly wider than in round 1 for the FOMC but still below 64%/3.5 because onsemi's own print is probably outside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$4.70 x 17x = $80), FCF yield (normalised-capex FY27 FCF ~$1.67B / ~395M shares = $4.23 at 5.25% = $80) and EV/sales (2027 revenue $7.42B x 4.0x less $0.595B net debt / 390M shares = $75), weighted 50/30/20 to give ~$79.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS is $4.53. I cut it ~7% to ~$4.20 for weak HV-EV/SiC (Infineon's weak HV drivetrain comment, NA EV sales -33% y/y in August, Chinese SiC wafer pricing), then roll forward with low-teens growth to NTM, a touch less than round 1's $4.80. Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.74 on 397M diluted shares and the $0.81-0.93 Q3 guide (Q2 8-K) support the recovery path. Synaptics (~13.6% more ON shares, closes mid-2027) is treated as roughly EPS-neutral in the window.

ON trades ~16.8x CY27 consensus today. Its closest auto/industrial analog peer, NXP, trades at ~15-17x forward; MCHP ~24x, TI ~32x and ADI ~30x carry less SiC/EV risk and more pricing power. With no clear re-rating catalyst inside 12 months (Synaptics dilution, a hiking Fed, and the HVDC ramp only from late 2027), I hold roughly today's multiple, 17x, instead of the 19x I used in round 1.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY2027 FCF ~$1.67B (OCF $2.04B less capex at 5% of revenue $0.37B) / ~395M shares = $4.23/share at 5.25%

inputs_detail.derivation: $7.42B consensus 2027 revenue x ~27.5% OCF margin (LTM 27%, slightly higher on utilisation) = $2.04B, less capex normalised to ~5% of revenue ($0.37B) rather than the ~2-3% trough, per the supervisor's finding.
Q2 non-GAAP diluted shares were 397.0M (basic 390.3M). Buybacks (~105% of FCF YTD) offset part of the dilution. Synaptics shares are excluded, consistent with the EPS-neutral assumption.
The market cap (~$29.6B) on LTM FCF normalised for 5% capex (~$1.36B) is a ~4.6% yield; on reported LTM FCF ($1.5B) it is ~5.1%. I use 5.25% to reflect the higher-rate backdrop (Fed hiking).

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 2027 revenue $7.42B x 4.0x = $29.7B EV, less $0.595B net debt, / ~390M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Cash $3,514.5M + short-term investments $350.0M less current debt $802.1M and long-term debt $3,657.3M at Jul 3, 2026 (corrected from $0.84B).
The current EV (~$30.2B) is ~4.1x 2027 consensus revenue; I hold ~4.0x while gross margin (39.3% in Q2) is still well below the 53% 2030 target.

bear.story: The EV slowdown deepens (North America -33% y/y, China -11%). Chinese SiC pricing erodes onsemi's SiC margins, and the peer auto recovery bypasses high-voltage power. The Fed keeps hiking (Oct 28 ~69% priced) and semis derate again. 2027 EPS ~$3.30 at ~14x.

base.story: The analog/power upcycle confirmed by TI, NXP, Infineon and ST carries gross margin into the low 40s. AI data-center revenue keeps growing off a small base, automotive is flat to up modestly, and Synaptics closes mid-2027 with little EPS effect. NTM EPS ~$4.6-4.8 at ~17x, in line with NXP's multiple.

bull.story: Consensus proves too low: utilisation passes 85%, gross margin passes 45%, and 800V HVDC design wins pull AI data-center expectations forward, so the stock re-rates toward MCHP-like multiples (~22-23x) on NTM EPS ~$5.3.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$52 (~11.5x consensus 2027 EPS and a ~7-8% yield on normalised FCF, levels seen only near cycle troughs, well under NXP's ~15x), the market would be pricing a new EPS downturn, not just a derating. That would most likely mean the cycle recovery peers report is failing for onsemi specifically: lost SiC traction share to Chinese or European rivals, a reversed gross-margin path, a guidance cut at Q3/Q4, or a failed or value-destroying Synaptics deal.

key_uncertainties: Automotive/EV demand: North American EV sales -33% y/y in August and China -11%. onsemi's automotive revenue fell 2% q/q in Q2.
SiC pricing and share versus Chinese substrate/device suppliers and Infineon/ST moving to 200mm.
Whether onsemi wins meaningful 800V HVDC share in AI data centers. Nvidia's named partners include Navitas, Infineon, ROHM, ST and TI.
Synaptics integration, dilution and regulatory timing.
Macro and sector multiple: the Fed hiked in September 2026 and ~69% odds of another hike on Oct 28; the SOX fell up to 29% from its June peak.
FCF durability: LTM FCF of $1.5B rests on trough capex (~2-3% of revenue); a return to ~5% capex costs ~$0.2B/yr.
reasoning: Round 2. Basic facts (Q2 2026 8-K): revenue $1,603.5M, non-GAAP EPS $0.74 on 397.0M diluted shares, GM 39.3%, Q3 guide $1.65-1.75B and EPS $0.81-0.93. LTM OCF is $1,672M and LTM FCF $1,500M, but Q2 capex was only $34.3M. Net debt is $0.595B (not the $0.84B I used in round 1). Consensus EPS is $3.20 for CY26 and $4.53 for CY27. The Synaptics all-stock deal (88/12 pro forma, ~13.6% more ON shares) is due to close mid-2027. Supervisor findings I accepted: (1) net debt corrected, worth ~+$0.6/share; (2) FCF capitalised trough capex, so I normalised capex to 5% of revenue, which cut FY27 FCF from $1.85B to $1.67B; (3) my 19x P/E exceeded ON's current ~16.8x CY27. I checked peers: NXP, the most comparable auto/industrial analog name, trades at ~15-17x forward, while TI/ADI/MCHP trade at 24-32x on lower SiC/EV risk. With no re-rating catalyst in 12 months, I cut to 17x. (4) The Oct 28 FOMC is in the 1-month window. The value-chain read is unchanged: the analog/power cycle has turned (TI, NXP, Infineon, ST), but onsemi's HV SiC/EV niche is the weak spot (Infineon HV drivetrain, EV sales, Chinese SiC pricing, Wolfspeed's negative GM), and HVDC revenue starts only late 2027. Methods: P/E $80, FCF yield $80, EV/sales $75, blended 50/30/20 to ~$79 (from $89). I keep my ~7% EPS haircut rather than dropping it; the supervisor found no source that settles it, and my lane's evidence (HV-EV weakness) supports it. Scenarios: 25% bear at $48, 50% base at $80, 25% bull at $120, a mean of ~$82. The ladder is a mix of lognormals centred on a median of ~$78 (85% weight at sigma 0.48, 15% at sigma 0.75 for fat tails), giving P(>=$76) 0.52 and P(>=$91) 0.38. Research was limited: two extra checks (the Q2 8-K and one peer-valuation search).
